agenda_text:
This Agenda contains a brief general description of each item to be considered. Copies of the Staff reports or
  other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of
  the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. Any person who has a question concerning any of the
  agenda items may call the City Manager at (310) 603-0220, ext. 200.

  Procedures for Addressing the Council

  IN ORDER TO EXPEDITE CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS, WE ASK THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO ADDRESS THE
  COUNCIL FILL OUT A FORM PROVIDED AT THE PODIUM, AND TO TURN IT IN TO THE CITY CLERK PRIOR TO
  THE START OF THE MEETING. FAILURE TO FILL OUR SUCH A FORM WILL PROHIBIT YOU FROM
  ADDRESSING THE COUNCIL IN THE ABSENCE OF THE UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL.

  AGENDA
  City Council Regular Meeting
  TO BE HELD ON

  February 4, 2020

  Duly Posted on 1/30/20 by MQ
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS - 11350 BULLIS RD, LYNWOOD, CA 90262
  6:00 PM

  1.  CALL TO ORDER
  2.  CERTIFICATION OF AGENDA POSTING BY CITY CLERK
  3.  ROLL CALL OF COUNCIL MEMBERS
  Aide Castro, Mayor
  Jorge Casanova, Mayor Pro Tem
  Salvador Alatorre, Council Member
  Marisela Santana, Council Member
  Jose Luis Solache, Council Member
  4.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
  5.  INVOCATION
  6.  PRESENTATIONS/PROCLAMATIONS
  Sheriff Captain Carter- Update on Law Enforcement Issues
  City Council Members Reporting on Meetings Attended (Gov. Code Section 53232.3 (D)).
  Good Samaritan Recognition
  Black History Month Proclamation
  LACS Team Recognition

  7.  COUNCIL RECESS TO:
  City of Lynwood as the Successor Agency to the Lynwood Redevelopment Agency
  Lynwood Public Financing Authority

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 1 of 135
   Lynwood Housing Authority

  PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  (Regarding Agenda Items Only)

  NON-AGENDA PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  THIS PORTION PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PUBLIC TO ADDRESS THE COUNCIL ON ITEMS
  WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE COUNCIL AND NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA. IF AN ITEM IS NOT ON THE
  AGENDA, THERE SHOULD BE NO SUBSTANTIAL DISCUSSION OF THE ISSUE BY THE COUNCIL, BUT COUNCIL
  MAY REFER THE MATTER TO STAFF OR SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVE DISCUSSION FOR A FUTURE MEETING.
  (The Ralph M. Brown Act, Government Code Section 54954.2 (a).)

  CITY COUNCIL ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
  CONSENT CALENDAR
  ALL MATTERS LISTED UNDER THE CONSENT CALENDAR WILL BE ACTED UPON BY ONE MOTION
  AFFIRMING THE ACTION RECOMMENDED ON THE AGENDA. THERE WILL BE NO SEPARATE DISCUSSION ON
  THESE ITEMS PRIOR TO VOTING UNLESS MEMBERS OF THE COUNCIL OR STAFF REQUEST SPECIFIC
  ITEMS TO BE REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR FOR SEPARATE ACTION.

  8.  APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated February 4, 2020 for FY 2019-2020. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the warrant register dated
  February 4, 2020 for FY 2019-2020.

  9.  PREVIOUS MEETINGS MINUTES
  Comments:
  N/A

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends the City Council approve the following minutes:
  Regular Meeting January 21, 2020
  Regular Closed Session January 21, 2020

  10.  TREASURER'S QUARTERLY REPORT
  Comments:
  The purpose of this item is to have the Honorable Mayor and the Lynwood City Council review the
  Treasurer’s Quarterly Investment Report as required by State Statutes. (CT)

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City of Lynwood receive and file the attached Quarterly Investment Report.
  The following information provided in this report highlights the investment activity for the 2nd quarter
  ending December 31, 2019.

  11.  STATE CONTROLLER’S RECOMMENDED INCREASE TO THE BID LIMIT
  THRESHOLD
  Comments:

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 2 of 135
   On November 1, 2018, the California State Controller issued a notification that the State
  Controller’s Office (SCO) recommended an increase to the bid limit threshold prescribed in
  Public Contract Code (PCC) 22032 effective January, 2019. Staff recommends that the City
  Council adopt a resolution to increase the bid limitations on public works projects in conformation
  to the latest SCO’s Notification Letter dated November 1, 2018. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled:" A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING THE STATE
  CONTROLLER'S RECOMMENDED INCREASE TO THE BID LIMITS FOR PUBLIC
  CONTRACTS."

  12.  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  AN AMENDMENT TO THE GENERAL AND MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES'
  CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION SCHEDULE
  Comments:
  A resolution of the City Council of the City of Lynwood approving an amendment to the general
  and management employees’ classification and compensation schedule. (HR)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO THE
  GENERAL  AND  MANAGEMENT  EMPLOYEES'  CLASSIFICATION  AND
  COMPENSATION SCHEDULE."

  NEW/OLD BUSINESS
  13.  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  AN EMPLOYMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT TO APPOINT THOMAS THORNTON
  TO THE NEWLY CREATED POSITION OF CITY ENGINEER
  Comments:
  A resolution of the City Council of the City of Lynwood approving an Employment Service
  Agreement to appoint Thomas Thornton to the newly created position of City Engineer. (HR)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve a resolution entitled "A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING AN
  EMPLOYMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT TO APPOINT THOMAS THORNTON TO THE
  NEWLY CREATED POSITION OF CITY ENGINEER."

  14.  APPROVAL OF AN AGREEMENT WITH RAMBOLL US CORPORATION FOR WELL
  11 ASSESSMENT
  Comments:
  Additional assessment is needed for Well 11. Staff recommends approving an agreement with
  Ramboll US Corporation for Well 11 Assessment because of their familiarity with the location and
  similar assessment work in and around the area. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING AN AWARD OF
  CONTRACT TO RAMBOLL US CORPORATION FOR WELL ASSESSMENT IN AN

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 3 of 135
   AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $75,000 BY WAY OF A 4/5ths VOTE OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  PURSUANT TO AN EXEPTION TO THE COMPETITIVE BIDDING PROCESS UNDER
  LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 6-3.13(a)(3); AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO
  EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT IN A FORM APPROVED BY THE CITY ATTORNEY;
  AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO APPROVE ADDITIONAL SERVICES NOT TO
  EXCEED 5% OF THE CONTRACT PRICE AND APPROVING THE APPROPRIATION
  OF $75,000 FROM THE UNAPPROPRIATED WATER FUND (FUND 6051).”

  15.  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST FROM NATIONWIDE ENVIRONMENTAL
  SERVICES FOR AN EXTENSION OF AN AGREEMENT ON THE MAINTENANCE OF
  CATCH BASINS AND THE STENCILING OF “NO DUMPING THIS DRAINS TO
  OCEAN” LOGOS ADJACENT TO THE CATCH BASINS
  Comments:
  The Agreement with Nationwide Environmental Services (NES) for catchbasin maintenance and
  stenciling of a logo “No Dumping This Drains to Ocean” is set to expire on September 30, 2020.
  Staff received a request from NES for a contract extension. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council consider a five-year contract extension and adopt the
  attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVING THE
  SECOND AMENDMENT TO NATIONWIDE ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES CATCH
  BASIN CLEANING AGREEMENT”.

  ADJOURNMENT - In memory of Kobe Bryant, Gianna Bryant and all others who lost their
  lives in the tragic helicopter accident.
  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING WILL BE HELD ON FEBRUARY 18, 2020 AT 6:00 P.M. IN THE
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS OF THE CITY HALL ANNEX, 11350 BULLIS ROAD, CITY OF
  LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA.

  SUBJECT:  TREASURER'S QUARTERLY REPORT

  Recommendation:

  It is recommended that the City of Lynwood receive and file the attached Quarterly Investment Report. The following
  information provided in this report highlights the investment activity for the 2nd quarter ending December 31, 2019.

  Background:

  Due to the crisis caused by the Orange County investment pool, the State Legislature in 1995 enacted SB564 and
  SB866. These laws were enacted as State Statutes to impose certain mandates regarding investments with public
  funds. The statutes have imposed the following mandates:

  1. Annual adoption of an Investment Policy that incorporates changes mandated by the State.

  2. Quarterly Investment Reports presented to the Legislative Body or Board Members.

  3. Restriction on the use of certain investment instruments.

  The purpose of the Treasurer’s report is to update the City Council and the public of the status of the City’s cash
  balances, investments and highlight changes from one period to another. This report includes reconciliation
  between cash and investment balances, a schedule of all investments, and a report providing information on all
  investment types, costs, interest rates, maturity dates and current market value.

  Reports prepared by FTN Main Street Capital Advisors are as follows:

  Portfolio Summary

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The market value of securities fluctuates, depending on how interest rates perform. When interest rates decrease,
  the market value of the securities in the City’s portfolio will likely increase and when the interest rates increase, the
  market value of the securities will likely decrease. The City’s practice is to buy and hold investments until maturity
  so changes in the market price do not affect the City’s investment principal.

  Short-term excess cash is primarily invested in the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) administered by the
  State Treasurer. LAIF is a high quality investment available in terms of safety, liquidity and yield. The City’s cash
  and investment portfolio is sufficiently liquid to meet expected expenditures for the coming six months.

  The majority of property tax revenues are received from the County in December and April. The vast majority of
  cash held by the City is deposited into the Local Agency Investment Fund and can be withdrawn at any time.

  There are three petty cash funds totaling $1,700.00 currently being used by various departments. There are two
  change funds totaling $640.00; Water Billing $600.00 and Recreation $40.00.

  The total amount of Non Sufficient Funds (NSF) from customers for the 2nd quarter reporting is $18,550.43 of
  which, $1,376.30 has been collected. The remaining balance of Non Sufficient Funds outstanding for the 2nd
  quarter is $17,174.13.

  The market valuation is provided by FTN Main Street Capital Advisors and all of the investments are in
  compliance with California Government Code Sections 53600 et seq. and the City’s investment policy.

  Fiscal Impact:

  The action recommended in this report will not have a fiscal impact on the City.

  SUBJECT:  STATE CONTROLLER’S RECOMMENDED INCREASE TO THE BID LIMIT
  THRESHOLD

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled:" A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING THE STATE CONTROLLER'S RECOMMENDED
  INCREASE TO THE BID LIMITS FOR PUBLIC CONTRACTS."

  Background:

  The California Legislature passed the Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting Act, Public Contract Code
  Section 22000 et seq. (“UPCCAA”). The Act provides public agencies economic benefits and greater freedom in
  expediting public works projects. Pursuant to the Lynwood Municipal Code 6-6.1, the City Council has elected to
  subject the City to the Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting Act in the performance and contracting for
  public projects.

  Lynwood Municipal Code (LMC) Section 6-6.14 acknowledges that the dollar amounts specified in the various
  provisions of Section 6-6 of the LMC are subject to periodic adjustment by the California Uniform Construction
  Cost Accounting Commission. Section 6-6.14 of the LMC includes a provision for the City Council to pass an
  ordinance or resolution to amend the affected provisions under Section 6.6 of LMC.

  On November 1, 2018, the California State Controller issued a notification that the State Controller’s Office
  (SCO) recommended an increase to the bid limit threshold prescribed in Public Contract Code (PCC) 22032
  effective January, 2019. (Attachment A)

  Discussion and Analysis:

  As specified in the State of California Public Contract Code, all governmental jurisdictions are limited to the dollar

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 80 of 135
   amount of public project work that can be performed using internal resources. The jurisdictions are further required
  to follow various bidding procedures in undertaking construction performed or contracted in the jurisdiction.

  PCC 22020 calls for the California Uniform Construction Cost Accounting Commission to consider whether there
  have been material changes in public construction costs and to make recommendations to the State Controller
  regarding adjustments in the monetary limits every five years. The SCO made the following changes effective as
  of January 1, 2019:

  a ) The change would allow projects costing $60,000 or less to be performed by employees of a public
  agency by force account, by negotiated contract, or by purchase order;

  b ) The change would allow projects costing up to $200,000 to be contracted by informal bidding
  procedures; and projects costing over $200,000 are subject to the formal bidding process.

  On September 15, 2015, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2015.165 adjusting the bid limitations in
  conformance to the SCO’s notification dated April 25, 2011. The following is summary of the current City’s bid
  limitations adopted on September 15, 2015 and proposed changes conforming to the SCO’s new bid limits:

  Resolution No.  SCO – New Bid
  2015.165  Limitations
  Public projects performed by public  $45,000 or less  $60,000 or less
  employees, by negotiated contract, or by
  purchase order
  Public projects subject to informal bidding  $175,000 or less  $200,000 or less
  procedures
  Public projects subject to formal bidding  more than  more than
  process  $175,000  $200,000

  Lynwood Municipal Code Section 6-6.14 includes a provision for the City Council to adopt a resolution or pass an
  ordinance amending the affected provisions.

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution to modify the bid limitations in conformation to the latest
  SCO’s Notification Letter dated November 1, 2018.

  Increases in the bid limitations provides the City a greater latitude in the execution of public works projects under a
  certain dollar amount resulting in expedited project delivery, reduction in the time, effort and expenses associated
  with bidding projects under $200,000.

  Fiscal Impact:

  There is no additional funding requested in adopting the staff’s recommendation.

  Informal Bidding Procedures as follows:

  SUBJECT:  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  AN AMENDMENT TO THE GENERAL AND MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES'
  CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION SCHEDULE

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO THE GENERAL AND MANAGEMENT
  EMPLOYEES' CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION SCHEDULE."

  Background:

  The City has a need from time to time to make adjustments to the Management and General Employees’ Salary
  Schedule, to add, delete and modify positions in order to meet the changing needs of the organization. The
  Municipal Code provides the City Council of the City of Lynwood the authority to amend said schedule by
  Resolution. In addition, in accordance with the Public Employee Retirement Law (PERL) any changes to
  employee compensation must be publicly adopted by the governing body.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The Personnel Rules and Regulations of the City of Lynwood grant the City Council the authority to adjust the
  salary schedule and add new classifications as needed to order to effectuate the business of the City of Lynwood.

  Staff is recommending the creation of a new classification of City Engineer. The Municipal Code of the City of
  Lynwood mandates certain functions be performed by the City Engineer. For example, the City Engineer has the
  authority to control traffic, parking, design of city assets, set development standards, call for the planting and/or
  removal of trees in the parkway and enforce industrial waste and water standards. The City Engineer must be a
  registered PE with the State of California in order to sign off on plans and permits issued to enforce the Municipal
  Code regulations. Generally, the Director of Public Works is also the City Engineer. The recent appointee to the
  Director of Public Works position is not an engineer and the City desires to create a new City Engineer position
  to ensure the proper enforcement of the Municipal Code and other regulations.

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 87 of 135
   In addition, staff is recommending the creation of a new classification entitled “CalPERS Retired Annuitant”. This
  new classification will be used to employ a retired annuitant who will be hired under Government Code §7522.56
  and §21224 and perform work of a limited duration in order to eliminate a backlog or work on a special project.
  Individuals employed as a CalPERS Retired Annuitant are limited to 960 hours in a fiscal year, may not receive
  any benefits or other renumeration other than salary, and can only be paid the salary equivalent to others
  performing similar work in the organization.

  The City Engineer classification is being recommended as an at-will management position represented by the
  Lynwood Management Employee’s Group (LEMG). LEMG expressed no concerns about the creation of the
  classification.

  The CalPERS Retired Annuitant classification is being recommended as at-will unrepresented due to the
  temporary nature of the work to be performed.

  Fiscal Impact:

  Any costs associated with the creation of these positions will be absorbed by the hiring department.

  AGENDA STAFF REPORT

  DATE:  February 4, 2020

  TO:  Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council

  APPROVED BY: Jose E. Ometeotl, City Manager

  PREPARED BY: Cynthia Stafford, Director of Human Resources & Risk Management

  SUBJECT:  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  AN EMPLOYMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT TO APPOINT THOMAS THORNTON
  TO THE NEWLY CREATED POSITION OF CITY ENGINEER

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve a resolution entitled "A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING AN EMPLOYMENT SERVICES
  AGREEMENT TO APPOINT THOMAS THORNTON TO THE NEWLY CREATED POSITION OF CITY
  ENGINEER."

  Background:

  The Municipal Code of the City of Lynwood mandates certain functions be performed by the City Engineer. For
  example, the City Engineer has the authority to control traffic, parking, design of city assets, set development
  standards, call for the planting and/or removal of trees in the parkway and enforce industrial waste and water
  standards. The City Engineer must be a registered PE with the State of California in order to sign off on plans
  and permits issued to enforce the Municipal Code regulations. Generally, the Director of Public Works is also the
  City Engineer. The recent appointee to the Director of Public Works position is not an engineer and the City
  desires to create a new City Engineer position and to appoint Thomas Thornton, Assistant City Engineer, to City
  Engineer, to ensure the proper enforcement of the Municipal Code and other regulations

  Discussion and Analysis:

  In a prior action, staff recommended the Management Employees’ Salary Schedule be amended to create the
  City Engineer classification. Based on the creation of the new position, staff is recommending the approval of a
  new Employment Services Agreement with Mr. Thornton appointing him to the newly created classification of City
  Engineer.

  Mr. Thornton has over 25 years of experience as an engineer and has worked with the City of Lynwood as our
  Assistant City Engineer since February, 2019. He has previously served as the Principal Engineer for the City of
  Adelanto, Senior Engineer for the City of Hesperia and as a Principal Engineer with the Western Municipal Water

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 101 of 135
   District. Mr. Thornton has a California Registered Professional Civil Engineer License.

  The attached At-Will Employment Services Agreement contains the terms and conditions of employment.
  Following is a summary of the salary and benefits:

  ·  Base Salary:  $158,000
  ·  457 Contributions:  $5,000
  ·  Employment Status:  At-Will
  ·  Health Benefits:  As provided other Management Employees of the City.

  Fiscal Impact:

  The cost of the difference between the budgeted Assistant City Engineer position and the City Engineer position
  will be absorbed by the Public Works Department for the remainder of the fiscal year.

  SUBJECT:  APPROVAL OF AN AGREEMENT WITH RAMBOLL US CORPORATION FOR WELL
  11 ASSESSMENT

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING AN AWARD OF CONTRACT TO RAMBOLL US
  CORPORATION FOR WELL ASSESSMENT IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $75,000 BY WAY OF A
  4/5ths VOTE OF THE CITY COUNCIL PURSUANT TO AN EXEPTION TO THE COMPETITIVE BIDDING
  PROCESS UNDER LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 6-3.13(a)(3); AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR
  TO EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT IN A FORM APPROVED BY THE CITY ATTORNEY; AUTHORIZING
  THE CITY MANAGER TO APPROVE ADDITIONAL SERVICES NOT TO EXCEED 5% OF THE
  CONTRACT PRICE AND APPROVING THE APPROPRIATION OF $75,000 FROM THE
  UNAPPROPRIATED WATER FUND (FUND 6051).”

  Background:

  Under the City Manager’s purchasing authority, Ramboll US Corporation (Ramboll) was retained to conduct an
  assessment of the source water near Well No. 11. Well No. 11 is located hydraulically downgradient of several
  industrial properties. Well No. 11 has experienced increased concentrations of chlorinated volatile organic
  compound (VOCs) in recent years, requiring the City to implement certain wellhead treatment measure. Ramboll
  has conducted initial borings at certain depths and ground water sampling at Beechwood Avenue and Flower
  Street; Flower Street and 3000 E. Imperial Highway.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  Outcome on the samplings taken at shallow and intermediate depths shows presence of VOCs. Ramboll
  recommends expanding the assessment to install a deep well to 310 feet within Fernwood Avenue, just
  downgradient of the current location. The additional scope of work includes: installation of a 300 feet deep zone

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 109 of 135
   well to investigate drinking water aquifer and forensic analysis of groundwater samples.
  Sampling at a greater depth is necessary for the forensic study. Ramboll’s cost proposal is $75,000 for this
  assessment. This amount exceeds the City Manager’s purchasing authority. Staff further recommends that the
  City Manager be given authority to approve up to 5% for additional services as needed.

  4/5ths Vote of the City Council Required for the Exception to Bidding

  Pursuant to Lynwood Municipal Code (LMC) 6-3.9(e), in non-emergency situations, departments should utilize a
  formal sealed request for qualification or proposal. Section 6-3.13(a)(3) of the LMC provides for an exception to
  this requirement if the City Council finds by 4/5ths vote of its members that the acquisition may be more
  economically and efficiently effected through the use of an alternate procedure.
  Ramboll has already completed borings at shallow and intermediate depths. The consulting firm has gathered
  historical data on uses in and around the study area. Staff recommends that further assessment be conducted
  expeditiously to assess contamination that may be affecting Well No. 11 by commissioning Ramboll to install 300
  feet deep zone well for this assessment. Accordingly, Staff recommends that the City Council make the finding
  that the acquisition of the services may be accomplished more economically and efficiently by awarding a contract
  to Ramboll than conducting an RFP process.

  SUBJECT:  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST FROM NATIONWIDE ENVIRONMENTAL
  SERVICES FOR AN EXTENSION OF AN AGREEMENT ON THE MAINTENANCE
  OF CATCH BASINS AND THE STENCILING OF “NO DUMPING THIS DRAINS TO
  OCEAN” LOGOS ADJACENT TO THE CATCH BASINS

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider a five-year contract extension and adopt the attached resolution
  entitled: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVING THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO
  NATIONWIDE ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES CATCH BASIN CLEANING AGREEMENT”.

  Background:

  In 2014, following a Request for Bids (RFB) process conducted by the Los Angeles Gateway Region Integrated
  Regional Water Management Joint Powers Authority (GWMA), the City Council approved a three-year
  agreement with Nationwide Environmental Services (NES) to maintain and clean the City owned and County of
  Los Angeles owned catch basins in Lynwood and to stencil “No Dumping This Drains to Ocean” logos near catch
  basin locations.

  In late August 2017, the City received a proposal from Nationwide Environmental Services (NES) requesting a
  three (3) year contract renewal with an option to renew. On September 5, 2017, the City Council approved a First
  Amendment to the Agreement with NES. The Agreement with NES, as amended, is set to expire on September
  30, 2020.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  MS4 Permit Requirements

  On December 28, 2012, the Waste Discharge Requirements for Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 127 of 135
   (MS4) Discharges within the Coastal Watersheds of Los Angeles County (Order No. R4-2012-0175) became
  effective. The municipal discharges of storm water and non-storm water by the Los Angeles County Flood Control
  District, the County of Los Angeles, and 84 incorporated cities within the coastal watersheds of Los Angeles
  County with the exception of the City of Long Beach became subject to waste discharge requirements as set forth
  under Order No. R4-2012-0175. The City is one of the 84 cities subject to the MS4 Permit. The MS4 Permit
  regulates municipal discharges of storm water and non-storm water from the permitees’ MS4s. MS4s is a system
  of conveyance which includes roads with drainage systems, streets, catch basins, curbs, gutters, ditches, or storm
  drains owned or operated by a State, city, etc., that discharges to waters of the United States.

  The municipal storm water and non-storm water discharges flow into receiving waters i n the Watershed
  Management Areas, including the Los Angeles River Watershed. The Regional Water Board has established
  Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs) to address water quality impairments. The City as a Permittee under the
  MS4 Permit is required to comply with Los Angeles River Watershed Management Area TMDLs as it pertains to
  trash, nitrogen, metals, and bacteria. For example the Trash TMDLs require each permittee to make annual
  reductions of its discharges of trash over a set period, until the numeric target of zero trash discharged from the
  MS4 is achieved. Other TMDLs specify that if certain water conditions are achieved this achievement constitutes
  attainment of waste load allocation.

  Catch basins are chambers, usually built at the curb line, which allow surface water runoff to enter the storm water
  conveyance system. Catch basins must be cleaned periodically to maintain their ability to prevent flooding. The
  removal of sediment, trash and decaying debris from catch basins help the City to comply with the MS4 Permit.
  Reminding the public not to dump into the catch basins also helps the City comply with the MS4 Permit. The City
  generally cleans about 616 City and County owned catch basins each year. Staff estimates that there may be up
  to 640 catch basins in Lynwood.

  First Amendment with NES

  NES has maintained the City’s catch basins since 2014. They are doing an excellent work. They also provide
  good documentation for the City’s annual NPDES report. They are responsive to the City’s requests. Catch
  basin cleaning has helped the City abate the amount of trash that may drain into the ocean as part of the
  requirements under the City’s MS4 permit.

  The First Amendment included the following terms:

  The term of the agreement extended to September 30, 2020
  The stenciling of the “No Dumping This Drains to Ocean” increased from $6 per logo to $7 per logo.
  The cleaning rate for each catch basin increased from $17 to $29 per cleaning.
  Price subject to an annual CPI Adjustment or 4% whichever is greater.
  The Not to Exceed Price per Year increased from $48,000 to $81,200.

  Request from NES for Second Amendment

  NES submitted a request to extend the term of the current agreement for five years under the same terms.
  (Attachment A)

  A Second Amendment to the Nationwide Environmental Services Agreement has been drafted (Exhibit A) should
  the City Council choose to award a five-year extension to NES.

  Pricing

  NES is not proposing any increase to the rate per cleaning with the extension. The rate per cleaning will still be
  subject to a CPI increase each year or a 4% increase whichever is higher.

  Staff conducted a survey of cities on the rate they pay for catchbasin cleaning. Cities responding to the survey
  either use RMI, the County, United Stormwater Inc., or NES. Below is a table on the current price per cleaning
  from cities that responded to staff’s survey and the current City of Lynwood’s rate.

  SUBJECT:  TREASURER'S QUARTERLY REPORT

  Recommendation:

  It is recommended that the City of Lynwood receive and file the attached Quarterly Investment Report. The following
  information provided in this report highlights the investment activity for the 2nd quarter ending December 31, 2019.

  Background:

  Due to the crisis caused by the Orange County investment pool, the State Legislature in 1995 enacted SB564 and
  SB866. These laws were enacted as State Statutes to impose certain mandates regarding investments with public
  funds. The statutes have imposed the following mandates:

  1. Annual adoption of an Investment Policy that incorporates changes mandated by the State.

  2. Quarterly Investment Reports presented to the Legislative Body or Board Members.

  3. Restriction on the use of certain investment instruments.

  The purpose of the Treasurer’s report is to update the City Council and the public of the status of the City’s cash
  balances, investments and highlight changes from one period to another. This report includes reconciliation
  between cash and investment balances, a schedule of all investments, and a report providing information on all
  investment types, costs, interest rates, maturity dates and current market value.

  Reports prepared by FTN Main Street Capital Advisors are as follows:

  Portfolio Summary
  Investment Policy Compliance Report
  Historical Earnings & Book Rate
  Portfolio Summary - Management

  Inventory by Maturity Report
  Credit Rating Report
  Interest Earnings Report
  Accrued Interest Report
  Gains/Losses
  Cash Reconciliation Report
  Monthly Economic & Market Update Report

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The market value of securities fluctuates, depending on how interest rates perform. When interest rates decrease,
  the market value of the securities in the City’s portfolio will likely increase and when the interest rates increase, the
  market value of the securities will likely decrease. The City’s practice is to buy and hold investments until maturity
  so changes in the market price do not affect the City’s investment principal.

  Short-term excess cash is primarily invested in the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) administered by the
  State Treasurer. LAIF is a high quality investment available in terms of safety, liquidity and yield. The City’s cash
  and investment portfolio is sufficiently liquid to meet expected expenditures for the coming six months.

  The majority of property tax revenues are received from the County in December and April. The vast majority of
  cash held by the City is deposited into the Local Agency Investment Fund and can be withdrawn at any time.

  There are three petty cash funds totaling $1,700.00 currently being used by various departments. There are two
  change funds totaling $640.00; Water Billing $600.00 and Recreation $40.00.

  The total amount of Non Sufficient Funds (NSF) from customers for the 2nd quarter reporting is $18,550.43 of
  which, $1,376.30 has been collected. The remaining balance of Non Sufficient Funds outstanding for the 2nd
  quarter is $17,174.13.

  The market valuation is provided by FTN Main Street Capital Advisors and all of the investments are in compliance with
  California Government Code Sections 53600 et seq. and the City’s investment policy.

  Fiscal Impact:

  The action recommended in this report will not have a fiscal impact on the City.

  SUBJECT:  TREASURER'S QUARTERLY REPORT

  Recommendation:

  It is recommended that the City of Lynwood receive and file the attached Quarterly Investment Report. The following
  information provided in this report highlights the investment activity for the 2nd quarter ending December 31, 2019.

  Background:

  Due to the crisis caused by the Orange County investment pool, the State Legislature in 1995 enacted SB564 and
  SB866. These laws were enacted as State Statutes to impose certain mandates regarding investments with public
  funds. The statutes have imposed the following mandates:

  1. Annual adoption of an Investment Policy that incorporates changes mandated by the State.

  2. Quarterly Investment Reports presented to the Legislative Body or Board Members.

  3. Restriction on the use of certain investment instruments.

  The purpose of the Treasurer’s report is to update the City Council and the public of the status of the City’s cash
  balances, investments and highlight changes from one period to another. This report includes reconciliation
  between cash and investment balances, a schedule of all investments, and a report providing information on all
  investment types, costs, interest rates, maturity dates and current market value.

  Reports prepared by FTN Main Street Capital Advisors are as follows:

  Portfolio Summary
  Investment Policy Compliance Report
  Historical Earnings & Book Rate
  Portfolio Summary - Management

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The market value of securities fluctuates, depending on how interest rates perform. When interest rates decrease,
  the market value of the securities in the City’s portfolio will likely increase and when the interest rates increase, the
  market value of the securities will likely decrease. The City’s practice is to buy and hold investments until maturity
  so changes in the market price do not affect the City’s investment principal.

  Short-term excess cash is primarily invested in the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) administered by the
  State Treasurer. LAIF is a high quality investment available in terms of safety, liquidity and yield. The City’s cash
  and investment portfolio is sufficiently liquid to meet expected expenditures for the coming six months.

  The majority of property tax revenues are received from the County in December and April. The vast majority of
  cash held by the City is deposited into the Local Agency Investment Fund and can be withdrawn at any time.

  There are three petty cash funds totaling $1,700.00 currently being used by various departments. There are two
  change funds totaling $640.00; Water Billing $600.00 and Recreation $40.00.

  The total amount of Non Sufficient Funds (NSF) from customers for the 2nd quarter reporting is $18,550.43 of
  which, $1,376.30 has been collected. The remaining balance of Non Sufficient Funds outstanding for the 2nd
  quarter is $17,174.13.

  The market valuation is provided by FTN Main Street Capital Advisors and all of the investments are in compliance with
  California Government Code Sections 53600 et seq. and the City’s investment policy.

  The action recommended in this report will not have a fiscal impact on the City.

  Money Market Fund - A Money Market fund is a type of mutual fund that invest in short term debt
  securities of agenies of the U.S. Government, banks, corporations and U.S. Treasury Bills.
  Some advantages of a money market fund over savings and CDs are high liquidity, low risk, and competive yields.

  Certificate of Deposit - A Certificate of Deposit or CD, is a time deposit. They are similar to savings
  accounts in that they are insured and relatively risk-free. They are different from savings accounts in that
  they usually are for a fixed term and a fixed interest rae. CDs are inteded to be held until maturity, at which
  time, the money may be withdrawn together with the accrued interest. The City currently has one CD
  within the City's investment portfolio

  Demand Deposits - Also known as "cash in the bank", this is the balance of the City's checking account with
  US Bank, from which virtually all obligations are paid.
